prd.title: Trust & Content Expansion Release Plan: Restore Free Access, Fix Billing Reliability, and Expand Workouts
prd.overview: User reviews reveal two high-impact trust problems: previously free or ad-supported content is being hidden behind subscriptions, and trial/billing flows are charging users unexpectedly or failing on cancellation. A smaller but critical group of paying users also reports paid benefits such as downloads and account login being unreliable. At the same time, the app's content is a clear strength: users value variety, warm-ups/cool-downs, demonstrations, and short beginner-friendly routines, and they are asking for new programs. This plan prioritizes restoring trustworthy access and payment behavior first, then builds on the content strength with new programs and exercise options.

findings.title: Previously free or ad-supported workouts are being paywalled
findings.summary: Many long-time and free-tier users report that content they previously accessed free or after watching ads now requires a subscription. Some say saved workouts are locked, and several describe being able to do only the first day or session before the app pushes a paid plan. The complaints span a wide range of ratings, suggesting high frustration even among users who otherwise like the app.

findings.title: Free trials lead to immediate charges and cancellation is unreliable
findings.summary: Users report being charged immediately when they sign up for free trials, and being charged after they have cancelled. Some also say they cannot find a way to manage or cancel the subscription either in the app or on the website, and one user says support submissions were rejected as spam.

uncertainties: Billing details cannot be verified; some charges may be due to misunderstanding trial terms rather than system errors.
limitations: Only a few reviews mention billing, and no purchase logs or account data were available.

findings.title: Free-with-ads tier is disappearing or unselectable
findings.summary: Ad-supported free access is becoming harder to reach in the app. One user says an update removed access to Free with Ads, another reports a premium-only pop-up with no continuation button even though the workout is available with ads, and one describes being hit with premium ads immediately on day two.

uncertainties: App UI and subscription flow may differ by platform or app version; these reports are from individual users.
limitations: Small number of reviews cover this specific UI problem.

findings.title: Paid access is unreliable: downloads fail and users get locked out of accounts
findings.summary: Paying users report that core benefits do not work as expected: workouts cannot be downloaded even with a paid subscription, and a user who was logged out cannot log back in to reach their workouts and paid benefits.

evidenceExcerpts.excerpt: even with a paid subscription, you cannot download.

uncertainties: Neither review explains which platform or account type was used; download behavior may be intentional for licensing rather than a bug.
limitations: Only two reviews cover this issue.

findings.title: Workout variety, short routines, and motivation are valued; users want more new programs and options
findings.summary: The app's workout content and motivation are strong assets. Users praise the variety, easy-to-follow routines, demonstrations, warm-ups/cool-downs, and short beginner-friendly workouts. Some explicitly ask for new programs and more exercise options, indicating content expansion is a clear opportunity.

evidenceExcerpts.excerpt: i love the warm ups and cool downs and demonstrations

uncertainties: Positive reviews may skew toward users who stayed engaged; this is not a measure of how many users want more programs.
limitations: Desired new programs are not specified in detail beyond 'new programs' and 'more workout or exercise options.'

requirements.title: Restore a clearly selectable free-with-ads access path for eligible workouts and plans
requirements.description: When a workout or plan supports ad-supported access, users without a subscription must be able to find and select that option without being forced into a payment flow. The app must not show a dead-end premium pop-up for content that is also available with ads, and previously saved workouts should remain accessible through the same ad-supported model they were saved under.
acceptanceCriteria: For any workout marked as ad-supported, a user without an active subscription sees a 'Continue with ads' button or equivalent option and can start the workout without entering a payment flow.
If the app promotes a subscription by showing a 'Free with ads' option, tapping that option does not dead-end and allows the user to select the ad-supported experience.
A saved workout that was previously accessible after watching ads can still be started via the ad-supported option after an app update.
A user on the free tier can reach at least one ad-supported workout from the home screen without encountering a subscription-only interruption.

requirements.title: End surprise paywalls and make free access limits transparent
requirements.description: Users should never discover mid-workout or on day two that content requires a subscription. Before a user starts a workout or plan, the app must clearly explain how many sessions are free and at what exact point a paid subscription or ad-supported option is required.
acceptanceCriteria: Before starting any plan, the app displays the number of free sessions or the specific point at which a subscription will be required.
If a workout is paywalled, the paywall is shown before the workout starts, not after the first session or day.

If a saved workout can no longer be accessed for free, the app explains the access change and provides an alternative action, such as watching ads, choosing a similar free workout, or reviewing subscription options.
Manual QA verifies that users are not asked for payment during a workout that was presented as free at the start.

requirements.title: Prevent immediate charges and mislabeled free trials
requirements.description: Anything labeled 'free trial' must never result in an immediate charge. Trial terms, including length, renewal date, and renewal amount, must be shown before the user agrees. If immediate payment is actually required, the offer must be labeled as a paid subscription rather than free.
acceptanceCriteria: Automated tests verify that signing up for a 'free trial' with a sandbox payment method results in a $0 charge through the end of the trial.
The trial sign-up screen shows trial length, renewal date, and renewal amount before the subscribe button is active.
No UI copy describes an offer as 'free trial' if the payment flow captures the subscription price at signup.
If a charge is required immediately, the offer copy must state the exact price and billing period up front, without claiming it is free.

requirements.title: Provide reliable subscription management and cancellation
requirements.description: Users must be able to view, manage, and cancel their subscription from the app or a direct link to the relevant store subscription settings. Cancellation must reliably stop future charges, and support submissions about cancellation must not be silently rejected.
acceptanceCriteria: All active subscriptions are visible in an in-app subscription management screen, or the app links directly to the platform's subscription management page.
A user can cancel their subscription without contacting customer support.
After cancellation, no subsequent charge is generated in the billing system.
Customer support submissions related to cancellation receive a confirmation and are not filtered out as spam.

requirements.title: Fix paid access reliability for downloads and login restore
requirements.description: Paying users must receive the core benefits they paid for. Workouts that are available for download must download successfully for active subscribers, and a user who is logged out must be able to log back in and restore access to their workouts and paid benefits.
acceptanceCriteria: With an active paid subscription, any downloadable workout can be downloaded successfully on supported platforms without errors.
A user who signs out and signs back in with the same account can access previously unlocked workouts and subscription benefits without contacting support.
An automated monitoring alert is triggered if subscriber login success rate or download success rate drops below 99.5% over a 24-hour period.
Manual QA verifies that a paid user can restore purchases after reinstalling the app on the same platform.

requirements.title: Release new workout programs and more exercise options
requirements.description: Build on the app's proven strengths in variety, beginner-friendly routines, demonstrations, and short workouts by releasing new programs and additional exercise options. This addresses direct user requests for fresh content and more workout choices.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one new complete workout program is published in release 1.1.0 and is clearly marked as new in the workout library.
The new program includes warm-up, cool-down, exercise demonstrations, and at least one short routine under 20 minutes.
The new program is accessible to both free-with-ads users and paid subscribers according to the app's access rules, with no broken paywall or ad-flow steps.
Active users can discover the new program from the home screen within two taps.
The workout library surfaces a 'More exercise options' or equivalent filter so users can see the newly added workout types.

versions.summary: Restore access trust and billing reliability: re-enable a selectable free-with-ads path, make free limits transparent, stop surprise trial charges, provide reliable cancellation, and fix paid benefits such as downloads and login.
Expand the workout library with new programs and more exercise options, continuing to leverage the app's existing strengths in short, beginner-friendly, and well-demonstrated routines.

tests.precondition: App is installed; user has no active subscription; at least one workout is marked as ad-supported in test data.
steps: Launch the app and sign in as a non-subscriber.
Navigate to the details screen for an ad-supported workout.
Confirm a 'Continue with ads' button or equivalent option is visible.
Tap the option and follow the ad-supported flow without entering a payment flow.
tests.expectedResult: The ad-supported workout starts successfully and the user is never forced into a payment flow.

tests.precondition: User has no active subscription; the app has a promotional entry point labeled 'Free with ads' for an ad-supported workout or plan.
steps: Launch the app and go to the home or subscription promotion screen.
Locate the 'Free with ads' option and tap it.
If prompted, select the ad-supported experience.
Dismiss any optional subscription upsell without purchasing.
Attempt to continue to the workout or plan.
tests.expectedResult: Tapping 'Free with ads' does not dead-end; the user can select and start the ad-supported experience without a required payment.

tests.precondition: Existing user account contains a saved workout that was accessible via ads in the previous app version; the app has been updated to the latest build.
steps: Install the updated app build.
Log in with the existing account.
Open the Saved Workouts section.
Tap the previously saved ad-supported workout.
Choose 'Continue with ads' and complete the ad if one is served.
tests.expectedResult: The saved workout still starts through the ad-supported option after the update, with no payment flow required.

tests.precondition: Fresh install; user is on the free tier with no active subscription; the home screen is visible.
steps: Launch the app and land on the home screen.
Browse the home screen content and locate an ad-supported workout card.
Tap the workout card and then tap 'Continue with ads'.
Start the workout.
tests.expectedResult: A free-tier user can reach and start at least one ad-supported workout from the home screen without encountering a subscription-only interruption.

tests.precondition: Non-subscriber; selected a plan that has a limited number of free sessions before a subscription is required.
steps: Open the plan details screen.
Read the pre-start information shown to the user.
Record whether it states the number of free sessions or the exact point where subscription is required.
Start the first session from the plan.
tests.expectedResult: Before the plan starts, the app clearly displays the number of free sessions or the exact subscription-required point; the first session does not hide a paywall.

tests.precondition: Non-subscriber; at least one workout in the catalog is fully paywalled with no free access.
steps: Navigate to the paywalled workout.
Tap the start or play button.
Observe when the paywall appears.
Do not complete a payment and attempt to exit the flow.
tests.expectedResult: The paywall appears before any workout content starts, not after the first session or day, and the user cannot start the workout for free.

tests.precondition: User has a saved workout that is no longer accessible for free in the current app build.
steps: Launch the app and log in.
Open the saved workout.
Tap start or play.
Read the explanation shown about the access change.
Choose one of the provided alternative actions, such as watching ads, selecting a similar free workout, or reviewing subscription options.
tests.expectedResult: The app explains why the saved workout is no longer free and provides a working alternative action instead of a dead-end.

tests.precondition: Manual QA build; test account has access to a workout that is presented as free at the start.
steps: Start the workout that is presented as free on its start screen.
Let the workout play through the complete session.
Watch for any payment prompt or subscription interruption during the workout.
Finish the workout without authorizing any payment.
tests.expectedResult: No payment prompt appears during the workout, and the workout completes under the free terms shown at the start.

tests.precondition: Sandbox environment; test user account; free trial offer enabled; billing ledger is accessible; sandbox test clock is available if needed.
steps: Automated test selects the 'free trial' offer.
Complete signup using the sandbox payment method.
Record all charges at signup.
Advance the sandbox test clock to the end of the trial period.
Record all charges through the trial end date.
Assert that the billing ledger shows $0.00 at signup and throughout the trial.
tests.expectedResult: Signing up for the 'free trial' results in a $0.00 charge at signup and no charge through the end of the trial; any post-trial renewal charge appears only after the trial end date.

tests.precondition: App is in the trial sign-up flow; offer includes trial length, renewal date, and renewal amount.
steps: Open the trial sign-up screen.
Before the terms are fully rendered, check whether the subscribe button is active.
Wait for trial length, renewal date, and renewal amount to appear.
Confirm the subscribe button becomes active only after the terms are displayed.
Review the displayed terms and compare them to the offer configuration.
tests.expectedResult: The trial sign-up screen shows trial length, renewal date, and renewal amount before the subscribe button is active.

tests.precondition: Test environment contains an offer configured to charge the subscription price immediately at signup; this offer is not a true free trial.
steps: Automated test opens the signup flow for the offer that charges immediately.
Collect all visible user-facing copy on the offer and signup screens.
Search the collected copy for the exact phrase 'free trial'.
Assert that the exact phrase 'free trial' is absent.
Assert that the exact price and billing period are displayed before signup.
tests.expectedResult: No UI copy describes the immediate-charge offer as 'free trial'; the offer is presented as a paid subscription with the exact price and billing period.

tests.precondition: An offer that requires immediate payment is available; it is not a true free trial.
steps: Open the offer that requires immediate payment.
Read the title, subtitle, and payment summary.
Verify the exact price and billing period are visible before any consent action.
Complete signup with a sandbox payment method.
Read the confirmation copy.
tests.expectedResult: The offer copy states the exact price and billing period up front and never claims the offer is free.

tests.precondition: Test account has an active subscription linked to the store/platform.
steps: Launch the app and sign in.
Go to Settings > Subscription or the equivalent management area.
Look for a Manage Subscription option.
Open the subscription management screen or the direct store link.
tests.expectedResult: The active subscription is visible in the in-app management screen, or the app links directly to the platform's subscription management page; viewing it does not require contacting support.

tests.precondition: Test account has an active subscription in a sandbox environment; store/platform supports user-initiated cancellation.
steps: Open the subscription management screen.
Tap Cancel Subscription or the equivalent control.
Confirm the cancellation when prompted.
Return to the subscription management screen and check the subscription status.
tests.expectedResult: The user can cancel the subscription without contacting customer support, and the status shows canceled or scheduled to expire at the end of the current period.

tests.precondition: Automated billing test environment; test subscription has been canceled; billing ledger is accessible; sandbox can advance billing cycles.
steps: Ensure the test subscription is canceled.
Advance the sandbox clock past the next billing cycle.
Inspect the billing ledger for any charge created after the cancellation time.
Assert that no new charge exists after cancellation.
tests.expectedResult: Cancellation reliably stops future charges; no subsequent charge is generated in the billing system after the cancellation.

tests.precondition: Support submission channel is available; a test user is able to submit a cancellation-related request.
steps: Open the support or contact screen.
Submit a request with the text 'cancel my subscription'.
Observe the confirmation screen or email.
Check the support inbox and spam filter for the submission.
tests.expectedResult: The support submission receives a confirmation and is not silently rejected or filtered out as spam.

tests.precondition: Active paid subscription; app installed on a supported platform; account has download entitlement.
steps: Sign in with the subscribed account.
Open the workout library.
Identify every workout marked as available for download.
Tap Download for each downloadable workout and wait for completion.
Record any download error or failure.
tests.expectedResult: Every downloadable workout downloads successfully without errors for the active subscriber.

tests.precondition: Account has previously unlocked workouts and an active subscription with paid benefits.
steps: Sign out of the account.
Sign back in with the same account credentials.
Open a previously unlocked workout.
Open the subscription benefits area and confirm the subscription is restored.
tests.expectedResult: After signing out and back in, all previously unlocked workouts and subscription benefits are accessible without contacting support or purchasing again.

tests.precondition: Monitoring system is configured with a 99.5% success-rate threshold for subscriber login and downloads over a 24-hour period; staging telemetry can be injected.
steps: Inject 24 hours of telemetry where subscriber login success rate is 99.4%.
Run the monitoring job and assert an alert is triggered.
Inject 24 hours of telemetry where download success rate is 99.4%.
Run the monitoring job and assert an alert is triggered.
Inject metrics at or above 99.5% for both rates and assert no alert is triggered.
tests.expectedResult: The monitoring alert fires when either rate drops below 99.5% over 24 hours and does not false-alert when rates are at or above 99.5%.

tests.precondition: Paid user account has purchases that can be restored on the same platform; app can be reinstalled from the same store account.
steps: Uninstall the app from the device.
Reinstall the app from the same store account.
Open the app and sign in.
Tap Restore Purchases.
Check previously unlocked workouts and subscription status.
tests.expectedResult: The paid user can restore purchases after reinstalling the app on the same platform without contacting support.

tests.precondition: Release 1.1.0 build is installed; workout library contains the program list from that release.
steps: Open the workout library.
Browse through the available programs.
Look for a workout program marked as 'New'.
Open the marked program and verify it is complete rather than a single session.
Record the program name and 'New' badge location.
tests.expectedResult: At least one new complete workout program is published in release 1.1.0 and is clearly marked as new in the workout library.

tests.precondition: Release 1.1.0 is installed and the new program is available.
steps: Open the new workout program.
Review the program session list.
Open the warm-up session and confirm it exists.
Open the cool-down session and confirm it exists.
Play an exercise demonstration video.
Locate a routine with a duration under 20 minutes.
tests.expectedResult: The new program includes a warm-up, cool-down, exercise demonstrations, and at least one short routine under 20 minutes.

tests.precondition: Two test accounts are available: one free-with-ads user and one active paid subscriber; release 1.1.0 is installed.
steps: Sign in with the free-with-ads account.
Open the new program and choose the ad-supported access option.
Complete the ad flow and start a workout.
Sign out and sign in with the paid subscriber account.
Open the same new program and start a workout.
tests.expectedResult: Both the free-with-ads user and the paid subscriber can access the new program according to the app's access rules, with no broken paywall or ad-flow step.

tests.precondition: User is signed in; home screen is visible; release 1.1.0 content is live.
steps: Start from the home screen.
Tap the first home screen surface that exposes the new program, such as a New Programs card.
Tap the new program card to open it.
Count the number of taps from the home screen to the program details.
tests.expectedResult: An active user can discover the new program from the home screen within two taps.

tests.precondition: Release 1.1.0 is installed; the workout library contains the newly added exercise types.
steps: Open the workout library.
Locate the filter or sort control.
Find the 'More exercise options' filter or the equivalent label.
Select that filter.
Browse the resulting workout types and check for newly added options.
tests.expectedResult: The workout library surfaces a 'More exercise options' filter or equivalent, and selecting it shows the newly added workout types.

assumptions.text: The product is intended to continue offering an ad-supported free tier. If that is no longer a business goal, req-1 and req-2 must be re-scoped.
assumptions.basis: Ad-supported access appears in current app promotions and user reviews, but no finding proves the intended long-term monetization model.

assumptions.text: The reported trial charges are unintended billing/configuration bugs rather than a deliberate pricing strategy.
assumptions.basis: Finding-2 is based on user self-reports; no backend billing logs or purchase records were available to confirm root cause.

assumptions.text: Downloadable workout content is already part of the current feature set, so the download failure in finding-4 is a bug to fix rather than a net-new feature request.
assumptions.basis: Finding-4 explicitly refers to downloads failing even with a paid subscription, implying the capability is expected.

assumptions.text: The handful of reviews asking for new programs represents broader content demand, but the exact new programs are not specified. We will validate program selection with in-app feedback before heavy content investment.
assumptions.basis: Finding-5 notes users ask for 'new programs' and 'more workout or exercise options' without specifying which programs; the sample is small.

limitations.message: Review text is not included in the provided statistics, so actual user-reported problems and opportunities cannot be directly extracted.
The provided statistics do not include cross-tabulations of rating by version, language, or date, so specific problematic versions or segments cannot be identified.
The language value 'other' is an aggregate and does not identify which non-English languages are represented.
The dataset is small (50 reviews) and spans only about one month, limiting the generalizability of findings.
No app-specific category or theme information is available, so product problems and opportunities can only be inferred from rating and distribution patterns.
